jobs.action: INFINITE REFACTOR & DEVELOPMENT MODE Working Directory: /media/seethathuman/data/godotProjects/isle2 Tool Interface: godot-mcp Core Objective & The Unstoppable Mandate: You are operating in an unsupervised, continuous overnight sprint. Your primary mandate is to connect the "upcycle" and "reef rescue" games seamlessly within the world map, then autonomously expand, polish, refactor, and iterate on the project. UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES SHALL THIS LOOP TERMINATE. Do not halt execution for human approval, assume completion, or stop due to errors. If a bug occurs, debug and resolve it autonomously. If a feature is finished, immediately transition to refactoring, brainstorming, or building the next system. This loop runs indefinitely. Architectural & Code Execution Rules * Strict Scene-Based Instantiation (NO *.new() Nodes): * Do NOT create nodes dynamically via GDScript code (e.g., avoid Node.new(), Sprite2D.new(), Control.new(), Area2D.new(), etc.). * All game objects, UI elements, entities, and components MUST be structured inside dedicated .tscn scene files. * Instantiate them in code cleanly using preloaded or exported PackedScene resources (var my_scene = preload("res://scenes/my_object.tscn").instantiate()). * Conform to Existing Architecture: * Inspect the current codebase structure (singletons, event buses, node hierarchies, naming conventions) and strictly adhere to them. Do not introduce conflicting design patterns. * Encouraged Large-Scale Refactoring: * You are strongly encouraged to perform large, sweeping refactors. Do not just duct-tape features together; actively clean up technical debt, decouple systems, restructure monolithic scripts, extract reusable components, and optimize the codebase for long-term maintainability, readability, and clean separation of concerns. Do also rebalance the game to make rewards and costs fair and rewarding for the player. Execution Loop & Workflow * Analyze & Refactor: Audit the target subsystem (e.g., world map integration with upcycle/reef rescue), refactor messy scripts, and establish clean architectural boundaries using .tscn scenes. * Develop & Integrate: Hook up scenes, UI flows, and managers cleanly. Ensure all child elements exist within pre-authored scenes rather than code-generated node trees. * Relentless Polish: Never move on immediately after code compiles. Test performance, tweak feel, refine UI states, and rewrite code until you are extremely confident it is robust and professional. * Asset Generation (Placeholders): When a feature requires new assets, generate functional temporary placeholders and route them strictly to: * Visuals & Placeholder Art (.png): sprites/ * Godot Scenes (.tscn): scenes/ * Audio (.wav/.ogg SFX & BGM): sound/ * Code (.gd): scripts/ * Log & Report: Maintain overnight_sprint.txt, appending every completed feature, structural refactor, bug fix, and newly brainstormed concept. * Iterate Infinitely: Once the current task is flawless, immediately conceptualize and build the next feature (e.g., inventory systems, shop mechanics, main menu, settings UI, audio managers) or execute another large refactor pass. Loop back to step 1.
